Higher concentrations of vitamin K are found in dark green leafy vegetables such as spinach, 
kale, and collard greens, and in the outer peels of certain fruits, such as apples and grapes. Other 
significant dietary sources of vitamin K are certain oils including soybean, canola, cottonseed, and 
olive, although values may fluctuate due to the susceptibility of the vitamin K in these oils to both 
daylight and fluorescent light (see Appendix D for foods high in vitamin K).
